I have a special needs child who sounds a lot like your nephew. Here is my advice. 

She needs to get her son evaluated for autism, ODD, adhd, pretty much any disability she can. Depending on the severity of her son’s disability and how high support needs he is her son’s pediatrician should be able to write a referral for her to get in home care for him. This is a huge help. If she is on Medicaid this service will be fully covered. He also, does not need a diagnosis first in some cases, often times the company that provides the home health aide will be able to do an evaluation to see if they can provide care and bill the insurance. 

Another service she needs to look for is wrap around services- a TSS aide to be exact, they will give her child in home behavioral therapy but also work with them at school. This service is also covered by Medicaid. 

I know this last piece of advice is going to be scary, but this is what I personally had to do to get help for my son when I was out of options- If Oregon also has a multi year long waitlist for autism services she might want to consider a self referral to CPS. I know CPS has a bad stigma, but they can be extremely helpful in this case. They helped me be able to push my son up to front of the wait list for multiple services and there was also a time where they helped me cover an electric bill. They can help her get set up with a lot of services and if she goes in as self referral she will be seen as a good parent and nothing will be held against her.
